picks.what: The Dam seen from the Zaan, etching (Rijksmuseum)
picks.who: Antoine Radigues after Jan de Beijer
picks.why: general view of the town front on the Zaan with the Oostzijderkerk tower; published by Pierre Fouquet; Rijksmuseum dates it only 1753–1800; margins and caption trimmed

picks.what: The town from the harbor, photograph
picks.why: exactly dated tourist photo of the waterfront with towers and church spire; sepia; curled dark print edges trimmed

picks.what: Windmills of the Zaanse Schans on the Zaan, photograph
picks.why: the town’s best-known sight, the mills De Kat, De Zoeker and Het Jonge Schaap across the river

gaps: P0, P1: nothing; P2: nothing firmly dated; P5: nothing usable
notes: 18th-century prints all carry Rijksmuseum date ranges only: Hendrik de Leth’s large panorama (#1, 1713–66, with a center fold) is the alternative to #7; #2/#6 (Radigues, ‘’t Inkomen van Zaandam’) and #3/#5 (other impressions of #7’s plate) are dated 1731–1809 or 1753–1800 on the same plates. #4 is a single church elevation, #8 a single house. P4 etchings of 1875–83 (#9, #11, #12, #13) show only mills and boats; #14 is a windmill sketch. P5: Mittelholzer’s 1931–32 aerial (#15) is mostly polder with the town far off; #16 is Zaandijk. P6: if a view of the town itself is preferred over the Zaanse Schans, #17 (2019 aerial from a plane, hazy) shows the whole city along the Zaan.
